memory_update.text: BWXT should remain the reference anchor for the advanced nuclear components and advanced fuel-fabrication node because it has direct naval nuclear, component, and TRISO-related evidence.
LEU belongs in the underfollowed lane as an upstream HALEU bottleneck candidate; it is not fuel fabrication itself, but many advanced fuel/reactor pathways depend on HALEU availability.
CW is a second-order nuclear component candidate hidden inside a diversified aerospace/defense and engineered-products business; verify nuclear revenue purity before upgrading.

LTBR is a speculative shadow candidate for advanced fuel technology and should not survive later layers without evidence of irradiation progress, licensing path, fabrication partners, and customer commitments.
Potential private or non-US-listed chokepoints such as X-energy/TRISO-X and other fuel fabrication assets may be more direct than listed equities, creating a public-market mapping gap.

node: Advanced nuclear components, reactor services, TRISO or advanced fuel fabrication, and naval/defense nuclear supply
summary: Expanded the universe around the advanced nuclear supply-chain node with a two-lane structure. The reference lane remains anchored by BWX Technologies because it is the clearest public-market mapping to naval nuclear components, TRISO-related fuel work, and nuclear lifecycle services. The underfollowed lane adds Centrus Energy for HALEU enrichment dependency, Curtiss-Wright for less-obvious reactor coolant pumps, valves, control systems, and naval/power nuclear components, and Lightbridge as a speculative shadow candidate tied to advanced metallic fuel technology. The strongest chokepoint evidence is in regulated fuel/enrichment and qualified nuclear components; the weakest is pre-commercial fuel technology where commercialization, licensing, and customer adoption remain unproven.
